correctness.rationale: Exact facet inequalities give precisely 12 vertices and 18 edges. All 220 triple determinants are nonzero, giving 134 spherical chambers by the Euler count. Exhaustive 4096 sign-mask arithmetic with exact primitive cross-products, exact cone feasibility and integer cyclic ordering yields 134 chambers in six explicitly tabulated signature classes. Spherical Girard area and Haar normalization give the three exact probabilities. An independent edge-angle computation confirms the mean. A standalone standard-library program executed successfully; numerical plane reconstructions and Monte Carlo are corroborative, not proofs.

value.rationale: A complete natural section-polygon law for a canonical non-centrally-symmetric Archimedean solid is a useful benchmark beyond a scalar edge-count expectation: it exhibits three genuinely possible types, six nontrivial spherical-orbit classes, and an exact pentagon majority of about 0.520247. The object and the observable are fixed by the solid’s natural incidence geometry rather than arbitrarily selected parameters. The probabilities resolve more structure than known face tables or mean counts; no wider theorem or broader claim is asserted.
